claims.text: At stage-3 DonHang.Api registers OutboxRelay<DonHangDbContext> with exchange donhang.orders (AddOutboxRelay); OutboxRelay derives from BackgroundService, so it runs as a hosted service in the API's process.
Each tick (PeriodicTimer, 1 s) opens a transaction and claims rows with SELECT … WHERE published_at IS NULL ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 20 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
FOR UPDATE locks the returned rows until the transaction ends; SKIP LOCKED skips rows another transaction has locked, so two copies of the API do not claim the same row at the same time.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: SELECT > The Locking Clause (SKIP LOCKED)

claims.text: RelayDueAsync sets PublishedAt only after await publisher.PublishAsync returns (lines 58-59); the finally block calls SaveChangesAsync and CommitAsync, so rows set before a failing publish are stored as published and the exception then propagates.

Confirms are enabled per channel (CreateChannelOptions); with confirmations and tracking on, awaited BasicPublishAsync completes once the broker confirms, throws if it refuses the message, and a publish while the connection is down throws.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ .NET client 7.x guide: Publisher Confirms (CreateChannelOptions, publisher confirmation tracking); examples/don-hang @ stage-3: RabbitMqPublisher.cs:16-20,48-50

claims.text: With publisher confirms on, RabbitMQ answers each publish once the queues the message is routed to have accepted it.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Consumer Acknowledgements and Publisher Confirms > Publisher Confirms / When Will Published Messages Be Confirmed by the Broker

claims.text: Without publisher confirms, RabbitMQ never acknowledges a publish, so a returned call says nothing about whether the broker kept the message.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Consumer Acknowledgements and Publisher Confirms (Publisher Confirms motivation); Reliability Guide > Publishers

claims.text: Exchange donhang.orders is declared Topic, durable: true (RabbitMqPublisher.cs:51); DonHang.Notifications declares notifications.order-events durable (RabbitMqTopology.cs:25); every message gets Persistent = true (RabbitMqPublisher.cs:28).
Durable exchanges and queues survive a broker restart; a confirmed message that RabbitMQ routed to a durable queue (persistent, or any message in a quorum queue) survives a restart of the broker.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Queues > Durability; Exchanges > Durability; Publishers > Message Durability; Quorum Queues

claims.text: broker-down.sh at stage-3: with RabbitMQ stopped, POST /api/v1/orders returns 201, the row reads 'order.placed | not published', the log reads 'Relaying outbox messages failed (...); trying again in 1 s'; after restart the row reads 'published' and the notification 'sent'.
ExecuteAsync catches exceptions from RelayDueAsync (unless stopping), logs one warning without stack trace and retries on the next 1 s tick; there is no backoff and no attempt limit for outbox rows.

If RabbitMQ is down, line 47 (connection.GetAsync) cannot open a connection, or line 48 (CreateChannelAsync) cannot open a channel on the one that dropped, so the first PublishAsync of a tick throws and the claimed rows stay unpublished.
If the process dies before COMMIT, PostgreSQL rolls back the open transaction when the session ends and releases its row locks, so published_at stays NULL and a later tick publishes the row again.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: Tutorial > Transactions; Explicit Locking > Row-Level Locks (held until transaction end); OutboxRelay.cs:41-42

claims.text: RabbitMqPublisher sets MessageId to the outbox row's Id (line 26), so a republished row's copies carry the same MessageId.

The outbox with a confirm-then-commit relay gives at-least-once delivery to the queues bound to the exchange: a confirmed message is not lost from them, but a row may be published more than once, so receivers must expect duplicates.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Publishers (republishing unconfirmed messages); Confirms (unroutable messages); prereq backend.l2.at-least-once-jobs

claims.text: The channel is opened on first use and reused while IsOpen; ExchangeDeclareAsync with the same settings changes nothing if the exchange exists.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: RabbitMqPublisher.cs:40-53; RabbitMQ docs: Exchanges (declaration is idempotent with equivalent attributes)
